aspect: The eligibility criteria exclude most people before they apply
description: Gaza residents may apply to visit first-degree relatives only if those relatives are dying, have died, or are getting married. Gisha's point is that the criteria are built so that the vast majority are never even considered.
energy_note: You may see your sister if she is dying. Not if she is ill.

aspect: Denial by silence is the commonest denial
description: Authorities routinely do not answer, or answer after the travel date has passed. Gisha calls non-response the most troubling form of bureaucratic violence, because there is nothing to appeal against.

aspect: EXAMPLE - one month of non-response, from one organisation's caseload
description: A woman could not visit a terminally ill sister. A man needing eye treatment in Jerusalem rescheduled six times. A couple postponed fertility treatment. A man was stranded in Gaza ten months, unable to return home. A young woman awaiting urgent cancer treatment filed six separate requests. All of them met Israel's own narrow criteria.
energy_note: Six applications for one course of cancer treatment.

aspect: The 'security block' rests on material you cannot see
description: Thousands are placed under security blocks that turn out to be arbitrary. The material is confidential and is withheld from the applicant and from her lawyer, so the case cannot be argued, only petitioned against.
energy_note: Accused of nothing, in a document you may not read.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the physician denied twice, cleared twice on the courthouse steps
description: A Gaza doctor applied in 2018 to reach Ramallah for Palestinian Medical Council certification exams. Denied on unspecified security grounds. Gisha petitioned the High Court; the ban was retracted before the hearing and the state was ordered to pay 3,000 ILS costs. February 2019, second set of exams, denied again on unspecified security grounds. The state withdrew immediately after the second petition was filed.
money_note: 3,000 ILS costs awarded against the state.
energy_note: A security threat twice, and not once the state would defend in court.
notes: The mechanism: a block that evaporates the moment it must be justified.

description: In seven petitions for Palestinian Christians denied permits to reach holy sites and family, the ground cited in all seven was 'overstay' - meaning a relative of theirs had at some point overstayed a permit. Gisha argues this is arbitrary collective punishment; it is also routine.
energy_note: Refused for something your cousin did in 2014.

aspect: The desperation is itself a lever
description: Gisha reports authorities exploiting applicants' need in order to extract information about neighbours or relatives. The permit queue doubles as a recruitment queue.
energy_note: The price of the permit is a name.

aspect: From January 2022 even the lawyers were cut out
description: The Gaza CLA refused to answer inquiries from human rights organisations and lawyers acting for Gaza residents - despite legal intervention often being the only route by which a permit is ever obtained.
energy_note: They closed the one door that sometimes opened.
